bull.b: Broad-based growth in both new locations and established restaurants indicates strong customer demand and a differentiated brand proposition. Sustained traffic gains provide a durable foundation for revenue expansion beyond menu pricing or footprint growth alone.

High unit productivity and continued openings suggest the Mediterranean fast-casual concept can be replicated across markets. Management's plan for 75–77 net new restaurants supports a multi-year runway for location-driven revenue growth.

A substantial liquidity cushion and positive operating cash flow give CAVA flexibility to fund restaurant growth, withstand cost volatility, and support operational investments. Improving cash generation also strengthens the quality and resilience of its profitability.

bear.t: Margin Pressure from Rising Operating Costs
bear.b: Higher food, packaging, and labor costs are compressing restaurant economics, while delivery mix adds expense pressure. Continued wage investment and fuel surcharges could limit margin expansion even if sales growth remains strong.

bear.t: Capital Intensity and Uneven Free Cash Flow
bear.b: Rapid restaurant development requires substantial construction and preopening spending, leaving relatively little cash after investment. Historical volatility means earnings growth may not consistently translate into distributable or balance-sheet cash.

The decline from unusually strong 2024 profitability shows that margins are sensitive to operating costs, mix, and investment levels. Lower returns on the growing capital base could constrain internal funding and reduce the benefits of scale.
